title: Knife claim challenged; Allegation of planted evidence a 'figment,' inquest told
article: The widow of Robert Scott Carpenter was accused Thursday of fabricating her story that an Amherstburg police officer planted a knife at the scene of her husband's fatal shooting.

"It's an absolute figment of your imagination," said lawyer Andrew Bradie during a heated exchange with Lisa Stewart that saw her maintain police were involved in what she earlier called a "cover-up."

The exchange came after taped interviews investigators conducted with Stewart were played at the coroner's inquest into her common- law husband's death. The interviews were taped Oct. 30 and 31, the day of and the day following the shooting at the couple's 258 McCurdy Dr. home.
Stewart makes no mention of planted evidence in either interview and makes statements that seem to contradict that version of events.

Stewart tells investigators with the province's special investigations unit that she saw a knife on the floor when she entered her home after Carpenter was shot. She says the knife, which she describes as a "switchblade," was open, but had no blood on it. Stewart then says she went outside and re-entered the house to find an officer standing around the knife.
Stewart told the inquest Wednesday she saw a police officer grab the knife from the fridge and place it on the carpet near the stairs shortly after Carpenter was shot.

Under cross-examination by Bradie, the lawyer for the officers involved in the shooting, Stewart said she didn't tell investigators about the planted knife because she was "afraid." She testified earlier that she had told investigators about the planted evidence although she couldn't provide specifics.

Bradie grilled Stewart for insisting her husband was shot by Sgt. Bart DiPasquale and not Const. Shawn McCurdy. Bradie said McCurdy has acknowledged being the shooter from the beginning. A ballistics expert testified the fatal bullet pulled from Carpenter's leg matched test bullets fired from McCurdy's service pistol.

In the two interviews played for the inquest Thursday, Stewart is adamant Carpenter was shot by a plain-clothes officer and not McCurdy. She testified again Thursday that DiPasquale fired the shot and that McCurdy never pulled his gun from his holster.

Asked to explain the forensic evidence, Stewart was given time to consult her lawyer. She then testified she had an "accusation" but not an "explanation" and said she saw Amherstburg police Const. Viktor Burany in the hospital operating room where Carpenter lay dead. Stewart identified Burany Wednesday as the officer who allegedly planted the knife.

She told the inquest that she entered the operating room with Carpenter's uncle, Arthur Kidd, a doctor with privileges at Hotel- Dieu Grace Hospital and saw Burany standing in the corner. She said she asked Kidd if it was possible the bullets could be switched and was told she was being "ridiculous."
On the tapes and in her testimony, Stewart also made allegations that two police officers "booted" her husband in the head after he was shot.
